privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.body: A document you upload is kept in Yomizaka's database (Toronto, Canada), visible to your account alone. When you ask for a check, the document, its text, or the PDF file, is sent to Orazaka, Krizaka's analysis engine, over HTTPS, and the result is kept with the run's id. Nothing is sold, shared or used to train a model. Deleting a document deletes its file, its text and its analyses. To ask a question or have your data removed, use the contact form.

sections.p: Krizaka, a company based in Montréal, publishes Yomizaka. The person in charge of the protection of personal information (Loi 25) can be reached through the contact form of krizaka.com. [TO BE COMPLETED: title and direct address of the privacy officer.]

Your e-mail address and a password hash (to run your account), the date you accepted the terms and this notice, the documents you upload and the results of the checks (to give you the service), and billing information handled by Stripe. We do not sell your information and we do not use your documents to train a model.

In a database in Canada. Documents are sent to Orazaka, Krizaka's analysis engine, over HTTPS to be checked. [TO BE REVIEWED BY THE LAWYER: mention of any transfer outside Québec and the privacy impact assessment.]

You can access, correct or delete your information, withdraw your consent and download your data by writing to the privacy officer. Deleting a document deletes its file, its text and its results. Closing your account deletes your documents. We keep invoices as the law requires.
If a confidentiality incident presents a risk of serious harm, we notify the Commission d'accès à l'information and the people concerned, as the law requires.

declared.observation: The photos declare the device “{device}” and the software “{software}”.
declared.mayIndicate: Nothing in itself: it is what the device or the software wrote when it saved the photo.

absent.observation: The photos declare no device, no software and no capture date.
absent.mayIndicate: Metadata removed. Messaging apps, screenshots and social networks also remove it by default.

noDevice.observation: The photos declare no capture device: most likely a screenshot or an export.
noDevice.mayIndicate: Nothing about authenticity. Noted because a photo of a paper document usually carries the device's name.

modifiedAfter.observation: A photo declares it was modified after it was taken: taken {taken}, modified {modified}.
modifiedAfter.mayIndicate: A later save. A rotation, a crop or an export from the photo library leave the same trace.

modifiedBefore.observation: A photo declares a modification date ({modified}) earlier than its capture ({taken}).
modifiedBefore.mayIndicate: Dates rewritten, or a device clock set wrong — which also happens after a time-zone change.

gpsRemoved.observation: A photo carried a GPS position. It was removed at upload and never kept.
gpsRemoved.mayIndicate: Nothing about authenticity: most phones write it by default.

batch.exportReadme:
Yomizaka — reports of a batch of checks.

lot.csv lists every row: its state, the reason when it did not run, and its file here.
rapports/ holds the signed PDF of each compliance check.
signaux/ holds the signals of each authenticity check, as Orazaka returned them.

These are informative checks, not legal advice. To verify a signed report, sign in to Yomizaka and open https://www.yomizaka.com/verify (only the people the report's owner gave access to can).
The Québec rules are still to be reviewed by a lawyer.

report.title: Audit report — {name}
report.disclaimer: Informative check, not legal advice. Yomizaka compares your document with published rules; it is not a legal opinion, and only a member of the Barreau du Québec can give legal advice. A result is never a guarantee of compliance.
report.summary: {failures} blocking failure(s) out of {rules} rules checked.
report.toReview: Québec rules still to be reviewed by a lawyer: a demonstration report, not legal advice.
report.modelValue: Chosen by the Studio, not reported by the run: the Studio and its version above are the trace.
report.noPassage: No passage: the document says nothing on this point.
report.guarantees: This report is signed with Yomizaka's key (Ed25519, held by Krizaka). The signature covers the document's SHA-256, the jurisdiction and rules version, the Studio and its version, the Orazaka run id, the date of the check, every finding with its passage and article, and the full text of this report. If a single character of this file changes, verification fails.
report.notGuaranteed: It does not prove that the findings are legally right: Orazaka applies the rules, the Québec ruleset is still to be reviewed by a lawyer, and this is not legal advice. It does not prove that the run exists on Orazaka's side (only its operator can say), nor when the report was made beyond the check dates above: there is no independent time-stamp and no blockchain. What you trust is Krizaka, the holder of the signing key.
report.howToVerify: To verify it, sign in to Yomizaka and open {url} — only the people the report's owner gave access to can, with their Yomizaka account. Give it this file and, to confirm which document was checked, the original document.
report.footer: Yomizaka, a Krizaka product — analysis by Orazaka.
report.signatureBody: SHA-256 of the report's text (pages before this one)
report.signatureNote: The attestation — the payload, the text fingerprint and this signature — is also embedded in the PDF file. A member the owner gave access to checks it by giving this file to the verification page; any change to the text of the earlier pages makes it fail.
report.notCheckedServiceContract: Not checked: the right to terminate (art. 2125 C.c.Q.) and the rest of the Civil Code of Québec on service contracts (art. 2098 and following). To be reviewed by a lawyer.

verify.title: Verify a report
verify.lead: Check that an audit report really comes from Yomizaka and has not been changed. Members only, for a report you own or were given access to.
verify.documentHint: Add it to confirm that the report is about this very file.
verify.empty: Give a report file or paste its text.
verify.okTitle: This report is authentic and unchanged.

reasons.NOT_A_REPORT: This is not a Yomizaka audit report: it has no signature block.
reasons.UNREADABLE: The signature block is damaged or not in a format Yomizaka knows.
reasons.BAD_SIGNATURE: The signature does not match the content: the report was modified or signed by another key.
reasons.ALTERED: The signature is valid for the original report, but the file is not that report any more: something was changed after signing.
reasons.UNKNOWN_KEY: It was signed by a key that is not this server's.
reasons.SPECIMEN: This report is a specimen: it proves nothing.

documentMatch.yes: The document you gave is the one that was checked.
documentMatch.no: The document you gave is NOT the one that was checked (its SHA-256 differs).
documentMatch.none: No document given: nothing says which file was checked except its SHA-256 above.

guarantees.a: The report was produced by Yomizaka's signing key, and not one character of it has changed since.
guarantees.b: It binds, in one signature, the document's SHA-256, the jurisdiction and rules version, the Studio and its version, the Orazaka run id, the check dates and every finding with its passage and article.
guarantees.c: Given the original document, it is the one that was checked.

limits.a: That the findings are right in law: Orazaka applies the rules, and the Québec ruleset is still to be reviewed by a lawyer. This is not legal advice.
limits.b: That the run exists on Orazaka's side: only its operator can confirm a run id.
limits.c: When the report was made, beyond the check dates it states: there is no independent time-stamp.
limits.d: Anything about the key holder: you trust Krizaka to keep the key. No blockchain, no third party.

verify.keyLead: Ed25519, SPKI in base64. With it you can verify a report without this site (for instance with OpenSSL on the signed text).
verify.devKey: This server uses the development key: its reports prove nothing.

landlord.title: Tenant application
landlord.lead: Ask an applicant's consent to check their payment history. They see the result first and decide whether to pass it on to you or contest it.
landlord.undertaking: I undertake to use these checks only to assess an application for a dwelling, to ask only what is necessary, and never to refuse an applicant on a discriminatory ground (Charter of human rights and freedoms; C.c.Q., art. 1899). I know an applicant may decline or contest, and that refusing to give unnecessary information is not a ground for rejection.
landlord.lawfulTitle: What the law lets you ask
landlord.lawful: The name, the current address, an identity document looked at without keeping a copy, the previous landlord's contact — and, with consent, a credit report. No social insurance number, bank details, employer or salary. Yomizaka offers no criminal-record check.

landlord.created: Hand this link to the applicant (it will not be shown again):
landlord.hidden: The result is visible only once the applicant passes it on.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.status: Draft: the refund policy and the clauses marked [TO BE REVIEWED BY THE LAWYER] are placeholders until a member of the Barreau du Québec has reviewed this text.

sections.p: Yomizaka compares a document you give it (a lease, an invoice, a service contract) with published rules and tells you, point by point, what it found, quoting your document. It is an informative check. It is not a legal opinion and it does not replace a lawyer: only a member of the Barreau du Québec can give legal advice in Québec. A result is never a guarantee that a document is lawful or valid.

You must give a real e-mail address and confirm it. You are responsible for your password. One free audit is included per account; creating several accounts to get more is not allowed and the extra accounts may be closed.

After the free audit, an audit costs the price shown at checkout in Canadian dollars, or you subscribe to the Pro plan. Goods and services tax (GST) and Québec sales tax (QST) are added at checkout and shown on your invoice with Krizaka's registration numbers. Payment is handled by Stripe; Yomizaka never sees your card number.

[TO BE REVIEWED BY THE LAWYER] Refund policy: placeholder. You can cancel the Pro plan at any time from the customer portal; the plan then ends at the end of the period already paid. Terms of refund for a single audit: to be written.
Your documents are kept in your account only and are sent to Orazaka, Krizaka's analysis engine, to be checked. See the privacy notice for retention, your rights and how to reach our privacy officer.
